tytul: No-cook strawberry syrup for the refrigerator (Cocktail Contessa recipe)
wstep: This card follows the Cocktail Contessa recipe for no-cook strawberry syrup: strawberries and sugar stand in the refrigerator, then the syrup is strained and must be kept refrigerated.

ostrzezenia.tekst: This syrup is never heated: NCHFP warns that uncooked jams mold or ferment in a short time at room temperature, so keep the fruit and the syrup in the refrigerator at every step.

akapity: The source is a drinks recipe, not a tested preserving recipe, so JarAtlas uses the shorter storage time it gives.
The US FDA list gives strawberries an approximate pH of 3.00–3.90.
Strawberries and sugar in a ratio of 2 : 1 by weight, that is twice as much fruit as sugar.
Sort and wash fully ripe berries, drain them and remove the caps and stems, as NCHFP directs for uncooked berry jam.
Put the strawberries and sugar in a clean jar and leave it in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours.
Sterilize canning jars and prepare two-piece canning lids according to the manufacturer’s directions.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): pour the strained syrup into a jar sterilized this way, close it and put it back in the refrigerator.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use the syrup within 10 days and throw away what is left; the source gives about 10–12 days in the refrigerator, and JarAtlas takes the shorter number.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): NCHFP says an opened container of uncooked jam should be kept in the refrigerator and used within a few days; treat an opened jar of this uncooked syrup the same way.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves.
